title: Signal Sets
outro_say: Next: scanning your watchlist with Prism.

steps.screen: The diagram with Signal Sets lit, then the Set editor
steps.say: A Signal Set turns readings into a decision: | Yes, No, or Unknown, with the reason.

steps.screen: The idea as a card: "Pullback in an uptrend"
steps.say: Here's a setup many traders look for: a pullback in an uptrend. | The main trend is up, but price has dipped in the short term.
Add the My Trend Group we built in the last video.
Add a single signal too: RSI, | which measures how hard recent closes have pushed up or down.

steps.screen: Writing two lines: "My Trend is Bullish" and "RSI is below 40"
steps.say: Now the decision. Line one: My Trend is Bullish. | Line two: RSI is at most forty, a short-term dip.

steps.screen: The "all of" box around the two lines; a hint of "any of" boxes
steps.say: Both lines must hold for a Yes. | For more flexible rules, you can add "any of" boxes.
Yes means every line holds. No means at least one fails. | Unknown means something needed is missing, and Lattice never fills it in.

steps.screen: The description, then Save as a new Set; the message "It now appears in Prism"
steps.say: The description reads your rule back in plain words. Save it, | and it's ready to scan in Prism.
Why it helps: instead of flicking through charts looking for dips in strong trends, | you get a clear Yes or No for every asset, with its reason.
